newsitem.title: UK: European bunker fuels soft Mideast, S.Africa steady.
newsitem.headline: European bunker fuels soft Mideast, S.Africa steady.

text.p: European bunker fuel oil prices were mostly softer in line with crude while diesel and gas oil bunkers eased with sharp losses in gas oil futures but trade at most ports was thin, brokers said.

Prices at Mideast Gulf ports held steady bolstered by active cargo trade to the Far East. Fujairah sellers asked between $113-115 for heavy fuel and $120-122 for light grades though gas oil related bunkers softened in thin trade.
South African markets were mostly steady with Durban 180 cst bunkers holding $119 and with diesel and gas oil at a premiums of around $20 and $30 respectively.
In Europe values generally drifted lower in seasonally thin trade but prices for diesel and gas oil saw biggest losses as IPE gas oil futures dipped by around $4 a tonne.
Rotterdam prices for 380 cst bunker fuel eased around $1 per tonne to $119-$121 delivered.
Dull trade in Hamburg markets pegged 380 cst bunkers back to around $122 while gas oil slipped a couple of dollars to $225/$228.
Mediterranean markets showed similar price tendencies but traders said small pockets of demand were supportive.
